scope: Decoder-worker staging and deferred screen-selection preparation for the M2 original-scan reopen workflow; not complete M2 acceptance.
changes: Verified worker-private Float64 mesh-coordinate chunks can transfer without first materializing an ordinary numeric array in the decoder worker. Public project values remain ordinary arrays and other carriers retain their existing behavior.

Screen-selection preparation begins on a selection gesture instead of when brush mode is enabled, avoiding a full scan copy when history restores a selected mesh. GUI and MCP retain their existing selection operations.
diagnosis: An instrumented prior PLY-3 run started screen-selection-worker immediately after GUI Undo and allocated a 266108040-byte Float64 copy. The worker-start event and allocation did not occur at that point after deferring preparation. Browser, graphics, renderer and artifact allocations also contributed to the guarded peak; the trace does not establish a single cause of all prior failures.

validation.fullSuite: 50568 passed, 76 skipped; 4 GiB job guard passed and cleanup confirmed. An earlier run failed three gesture tests due to an optional viewport object-map lookup; the final source passed those focused tests and the full rerun.
validation.build: All 14 typecheck batches and the production build passed under the 4 GiB guard.
validation.selection: Thirty focused selection, gesture and MCP tests passed. A separate browser replay compared actual GUI gestures with public MCP for rectangle, circle, brush, freehand and line on point clouds and meshes, including subtraction and history.
validation.decoder: Thirteen private Float64 decoding tests cover carriers, aliases, signed zero, borrowed buffers and invalid input. A real browser decoder-worker check verified returned arrays, aliases, cancellation and worker termination.
validation.originalPly3: The exact final build ran GUI Split and Extract, public MCP artifact export and complete download, GUI in-place project reopen, geometry digests, and GUI Undo/Redo after reopen. Source, cutter and output geometry matched; input had 3691133 facets and output had 3695945 facets. The 4 GiB job guard passed at 4219797504 bytes with cleanup confirmed. An earlier untraced combined candidate passed at 4268969984 bytes; an instrumented run completed the workflow but exceeded the guard at 4297043968 bytes. These are separate runs and do not establish a general memory bound.
validation.combinedPreview: The two changes were applied to the existing combined preview without replacing other task work. Forty-six focused tests and a real decoder-worker browser check passed from that checkout. The original PLY-3 replay used the M2 candidate build, not the combined preview.

limitations: A separate transport diagnostic reproduced stale numeric-array reuse when an already-selected candidate is mutated during a later asynchronous lookup. The diagnostic exercises a low-level callback and does not establish that a normal GUI or MCP action can trigger the mutation; restore safety remains open.
The PLY-3 peak has less than 72 MiB headroom and a previous instrumented run exceeded the guard. Repeated runs do not guarantee all large projects fit.
Native rotated Split differs on a retained control, and broader M2 native, lifecycle and resource gates remain open.
